reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of decentralized exploration lies in balancing collective learning with individual privacy. Each player asynchronously interacts with a shared stochastic environment, aiming to identify the best arm without revealing personal data. The DECENTRALIZED ELIMINATION algorithm acts as a kernel, enabling any best-arm identification method to function in a distributed setting. It operates under the constraint that players must communicate only binary messages indicating arm elimination. This leads to a trade-off between communication cost and sample efficiency, where the penalty scales inversely with the square of the most frequent player's activity probability. The ε-optimal arm definition provides a quantifiable measure of near-optimality, allowing for probabilistic guarantees on convergence. Privacy is enforced by bounding the information an adversary can extract from intercepted messages, modeled via mutual information. These primitives form a dual structure: one for inference (GSI) and one for action (GSE), both grounded in stochastic optimization and information theory.
